target_customer: Consumers buying secondary market event tickets; revenue came from partner brokers
problem: Secondary ticket prices were scattered across brokers and exchanges; TicketStumbler aggregated listings so buyers could compare seats and prices.
business_model: Affiliate commission, 6 to 15 percent of sales completed on partner broker sites

founders.name: Tom Davis
previous_startups: Swaptitude (later project, per a wiki mirror)
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and in TechCrunch August 2008.

founders.name: Dan Haubert
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and in TechCrunch August 2008.

exit.reason: A wiki mirror says the site was shut down after Dan Haubert died unexpectedly; not independently confirmed.

competitors.name: Tickex
competitors.what: Ticket search that also covered concerts

competitors.name: FanSnap
competitors.what: Palo Alto ticket search engine aggregating more than 50 providers
competitors.traction_then: Described in October 2008 as a new startup and the third aggregator site

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating thousands of listings from hundreds of brokers needed scraping and feed integrations and normalized seat data, which is more than basic CRUD.

defensibility.rationale: Listings came from third parties and aggregation was copyable; success depended on listing breadth and broker deals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acted against it; later rivals FanSnap and SeatGeek consolidated, with SeatGeek buying FanSnap in 2013.

market_need_then: Secondary ticket prices varied across StubHub, brokers and exchanges, and TechCrunch noted few contenders in August 2008, but no usage figures for TicketStumbler were found.

branding.domain_note: ticketstumbler.com did not resolve from the research environment; a wiki mirror says it later linked to Tom Davis's Swaptitude project.
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch launch coverage in August 2008 and a mention in a February 2009 Fortune piece on ticket resellers; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A playful name echoing StumbleUpon style discovery and a couple of press mentions, but no evidence of consumer loyalty.

outcome_analysis: TicketStumbler launched in August 2008 from Boston as a secondary ticket comparison engine paid by broker commissions. The only account of its end, a single wiki mirror, says it closed after co-founder Dan Haubert died unexpectedly, which is a personal event outside the usual taxonomy, so the factor is other; the account is unverified and the competitive field of FanSnap, SeatGeek and others was growing at the time.
notes: The 15,000 dollar June 2008 seed rests on one wiki mirror (the ipfs copy of a Wikipedia style article), whose snippet did not name the investor; TechCrunch only says TicketStumbler is a Y Combinator startup. The shutdown cause and Swaptitude link are single source and unverified. The ipfs page itself could not be fetched (HTTP 418), so these details come from search summaries. FanSnap source is October 2008, within the batch period.
